## Setup: Example Data

All examples in this document use the `patients` dataset created below.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)

set.seed(42)

n <- 40

patients <- tibble(
  pt_id     = paste0("P", sprintf("%03d", 1:n)),
  gender    = sample(c("M", "F"), n, replace = TRUE),
  height    = round(rnorm(n, mean = 168, sd = 10)),
  weight    = round(rnorm(n, mean = 70,  sd = 15)),
  Age       = round(runif(n, min = 30, max = 72)),
  Diagnosis = sample(c("Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Healthy"),
                     n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.35, 0.35, 0.30)),
  disease   = Diagnosis,
  HbA1c     = round(
    case_when(
      Diagnosis == "Diabetes"     ~ rnorm(n, mean = 8.0, sd = 1.0),
      Diagnosis == "Hypertension" ~ rnorm(n, mean = 5.8, sd = 0.7),
      TRUE                        ~ rnorm(n, mean = 5.2, sd = 0.5)
    ), 1)
)

# data.frame version for comparison
patients_df <- as.data.frame(patients)

patients
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## tidyverse

`tidyverse` is a meta-package that includes useful packages such as `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, and `tidyr`.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# install (once)
install.packages("tidyverse")
```

```{r}
#| message: false
# load every session
library(tidyverse)
```

### data.frame vs. tibble

`tibble` is an improved version of `data.frame` that displays column types on print and handles large datasets cleanly.

```{r}
# data.frame: prints all rows, no type info
patients_df

# tibble: shows type tags (<chr>, <dbl>, ...) and caps output at 10 rows
patients
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Chain operator (`%>%`)

```{r}
# traditional style
head(patients)

# chain style (Ctrl + Shift + M)
patients %>% head()
```

## 1. Data Wrangling: dplyr

### The 5 core dplyr verbs

#### select(): select columns

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_select.png){fig-align="center" width="164"}

```{r}
patients %>% select(pt_id, disease)
```

#### filter(): filter rows

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_fjilter.png){fig-align="center" width="180"}

```{r}
patients %>% filter(disease == "Diabetes")
```

#### mutate(): create new columns

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_mutate.png){fig-align="center" width="211"}

```{r}
patients %>% mutate(bmi = round(weight / (height / 100)^2, 1))
```

#### arrange(): sort rows

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_arrange.png){fig-align="center" width="204"}

```{r}
patients %>% arrange(desc(weight))
```

#### group_by() & summarise(): group-wise summary

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_group_by.png){fig-align="center" width="258"}

```{r}
patients %>%
  group_by(disease) %>%
  summarize(
    n           = n(),
    mean_weight = round(mean(weight), 1),
    mean_HbA1c  = round(mean(HbA1c),  1)
  )
```

### join: combining datasets

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_join.png){fig-align="center" width="251"}

```{r}
# lab results — some patients missing, one external patient included
lab_results <- tibble(
  pt_id = c("P001", "P002", "P003", "P999"),
  hba1c = c(7.5, 5.8, 6.2, 8.0)
)
```

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_left.png){fig-align="center"}

```{r}
# left_join: keep all patients in the cohort
patients %>%
  select(pt_id, disease) %>%
  left_join(lab_results, by = "pt_id")
```

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_right.png){fig-align="center" width="112"}

```{r}
# right_join: based on lab results
patients %>%
  select(pt_id, disease) %>%
  right_join(lab_results, by = "pt_id")
```

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_inner.png){fig-align="center" width="123"}

```{r}
# inner_join: intersection (only patients with lab results)
patients %>%
  select(pt_id, disease) %>%
  inner_join(lab_results, by = "pt_id")
```

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_full.png){fig-align="center"}

```{r}
# full_join: merge all data
patients %>%
  select(pt_id, disease) %>%
  full_join(lab_results, by = "pt_id")
```

### Data Reshaping: tidyr

#### pivot_longer(): Wide → Long

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_pivet_long.png){fig-align="center" width="390"}

```{r}
bp_wide <- tibble(
  pt_id      = c("P001", "P002", "P003"),
  sbp_visit1 = c(120, 130, 110),
  sbp_visit2 = c(118, 135, 115),
  sbp_visit3 = c(115, 132, 112)
)

bp_wide

bp_long <- bp_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = starts_with("sbp"),
    names_to  = "visit",
    values_to = "sbp"
  )

bp_long
```

#### pivot_wider(): Long → Wide

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_pivot_wider.png){fig-align="center"}

```{r}
bp_long %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = visit,
    values_from = sbp
  )
```

#### separate(): split a column

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_separate.png){fig-align="center" width="482"}

```{r}
bp_raw <- tibble(
  pt_id   = c("P001", "P002"),
  bp_full = c("120/80", "130/85")
)

bp_raw %>%
  separate(bp_full, into = c("sbp", "dbp"), sep = "/", convert = TRUE)
```

#### unite(): merge columns

![](/assets/img/part1/W3_unite.png){fig-align="center" width="351"}

```{r}
dates <- tibble(
  pt_id = c("P001", "P002"),
  year  = c("2024", "2025"),
  month = c("12", "01"),
  day   = c("25", "15")
)

dates %>%
  unite(col = "exam_date", year, month, day, sep = "-")
```

## 2. Visualization: ggplot2

ggplot2 is built on three components:

1)  **data**: a data frame
2)  **aes**: x-axis, y-axis, color, fill, group, etc.
3)  **geom**: the type of plot

```{r}
#| eval: false
dataframe %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = xx, y = yy)) +
  geom_function() +
  ...
```

#### Aesthetics

| Property         | Description       | Example                           |
|------------------|-------------------|-----------------------------------|
| `color` / `fill` | Color             | `"red"`, `"#RRGGBB"`              |
| `linetype`       | Line type         | `"solid"`, `"dashed"`, `"dotted"` |
| `size`           | Point / text size | in mm                             |
| `linewidth`      | Line width        | in mm                             |
| `shape`          | Point shape       | integer 0–25                      |
| `alpha`          | Transparency      | 0 (transparent) – 1 (opaque)      |

::: callout-tip
**Inside `aes()`**: maps to a variable automatically → `aes(color = Diagnosis)`

**Inside `geom_`**: fixed value → `geom_bar(color = 'black')`
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ① Bar Plot: frequency of categorical data

```{r}
patients %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Number of Patients by Diagnosis",
       x = "Diagnosis", y = "Count") +
  theme_classic()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ② Histogram: distribution of a continuous variable

```{r}
patients %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 10, fill = "lightgrey", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution", x = "Age", y = "Count") +
  theme_classic()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ③ Box Plot: comparing continuous values across groups

```{r}
patients %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Diagnosis, y = HbA1c, fill = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "HbA1c by Diagnosis", x = "Diagnosis", y = "HbA1c (%)") +
  theme_classic()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ④ Scatter Plot: relationship between two continuous variables

```{r}
#| message: false
patients %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = HbA1c)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = 'darkblue') +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Age vs HbA1c", x = "Age", y = "HbA1c (%)") +
  theme_classic()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### ⑤ Line Plot: trends over time

```{r}
bp_long %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = visit, y = sbp, group = pt_id, color = pt_id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Systolic BP Across Visits",
       x = "Visit", y = "SBP (mmHg)", color = "Patient") +
  theme_classic()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Customizing Plots

```{r}
patients %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Diagnosis, y = HbA1c, fill = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "HbA1c Levels by Diagnosis",
       x = "Diagnosis", y = "HbA1c (%)") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  theme_classic()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Key Themes

| Theme             | Description                   |
|-------------------|-------------------------------|
| `theme_classic()` | White background, axes only   |
| `theme_bw()`      | White background + grid lines |
| `theme_minimal()` | Minimal decoration            |
| `theme_light()`   | Light tone                    |

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 3
#| message: false
p <- patients %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Diagnosis, y = HbA1c, fill = Diagnosis)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

library(patchwork)
(p + theme_classic()  + ggtitle("theme_classic()")) +
(p + theme_bw()       + ggtitle("theme_bw()")) +
(p + theme_minimal()  + ggtitle("theme_minimal()")) +
(p + theme_light()    + ggtitle("theme_light()"))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Saving Plots

```{r}
#| eval: false
# format determined automatically by file extension
ggsave("results/w3_my_result.png")

# high-resolution TIFF (for publication)
ggsave("results/w3_Figure1.tiff",
       width = 6, height = 4, units = "in", dpi = 300)

# PDF (for presentations; scales without pixelation)
ggsave("results/w3_Figure1.pdf", width = 6, height = 4)
```
